meta: The final part of "Inside AI's brain". Earlier parts showed AI answers by guessing word by word, and whatever comes out stays. For hard problems, that leads to mistakes. Meet reasoning models.

muc.title: Answering right away leads to mistakes
muc.text: The last part. So far, AI answers by guessing word by word, and whatever comes out stays. For hard problems, answering right away leads to mistakes.

muc.title: Scratch paper
muc.text: Reasoning models are taught one more thing: write a draft first. Break the problem into steps, try one way, check it, fix mistakes, and only then give the answer.

muc.title: Fast or careful?
muc.text: The trade-off is that it's slower and costs more. Simple questions don't need it. But for math, planning and comparing many options, thinking mode is much better.

muc.title: Turn on thinking mode
muc.text: For hard questions, turn on thinking mode in your chat app. For simple ones, turn it off to save time.

muc.title: 8 pieces of AI's brain
muc.text: And that's the whole of AI's brain. Cut text into pieces. Put meaning on a map. Pay attention to the right places. Read a whole library. Get taught how to answer by people. Draw each word. Read your documents. And think before speaking.

muc.title: Next series
muc.text: Now that you understand AI, it's time to turn it into your own assistant. That's the next series.
